necessary_context.content: At each time t choose arm A_t in {1,...,K} using the available past and obtain a fresh independent reward from its distribution. The source defines a strategy by a predictable sampling rule, a stopping time tau and a terminal measurable arm recommendation.
necessary_context.name: Sequential sampling model

necessary_context.content: d nu_theta/d xi(x)=exp(theta*x-b(theta)), theta in Theta subset R; b is convex and twice differentiable. The source assumes the distribution can be uniquely indexed by its mean mu=b'(theta). For means mu=b'(theta), lambda=b'(theta'), d(mu,lambda)=KL(nu^mu,nu^lambda)=b(theta')-b(theta)-b'(theta)(theta'-theta).
necessary_context.name: Canonical exponential family and divergence

necessary_context.content: S is a set of exponential-family bandit models with unique best arm a*(mu). A delta-PAC strategy satisfies, for every mu in S, P_mu(tau_delta<infinity)=1 and P_mu(recommendation != a*(mu))<=delta. Alt(mu)={lambda in S:a*(lambda)!=a*(mu)}; Sigma_K is the probability simplex. Theorem 1 initially permits a general such S; p.4 subsequently fixes S to all models with a unique best arm for the rest of the paper.
necessary_context.name: PAC and alternatives
